output.summary: KEP-2799 proposed stopping the Token Controller from auto-generating secret-based service account tokens and later purging unused auto-generated ones, while keeping explicitly requested secret tokens. The KEP reached implemented status at stable stage.
output.rationale: BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume went GA in 1.22, so pod tokens come from the TokenRequest API and auto-generated secret tokens are no longer needed. Those secrets are less secure than bound tokens, so the KEP stops auto-creating them. Reviewers required that cleanup not break existing users, so deletion is limited to unreferenced tokens unused for a long period, with usage tracking first.

alternatives.option: Remove or limit explicitly requested secret-based tokens too
alternatives.why_not: Non-goal in the readme: "Removal of explicitly requested secret-based service account tokens" is out of scope, and reviewers noted explicit tokens are part of the workload API.

alternatives.option: Add per-namespace or per-service-account knobs to control auto-generated secrets
alternatives.why_not: liggitt in rcomment:705717728: "Per-namespace or per-serviceaccount controls around auto-generated secrets expose APIs I don't think we want long-term."

alternatives.option: Delete auto-generated tokens immediately with a single release-based cleanup
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers wanted upgrades to stay safe: "upgrading must remain as safe and non-disruptive as possible for users" (rcomment:706149814). Cleanup was gated on usage tracking and a sufficient period of non-use instead.
zshihang (rcomment:675078384) argued the name "might not describe the phase correctly" because the gate removes TokenController from the tree.

evidence.quote: As BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume is GA in 1.22, pods’ service account tokens would be obtained via TokenRequest API and stored as projected volume.
Change the service account control loop in Token Controller to not auto-create secret for service accounts.
upgrading must remain as safe and non-disruptive as possible for users. To that end, we should only clean up auto-generated tokens which
if LegacyServiceAccountTokenTracking is disabled, LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp would not clean up tokens because it cannot determine `last-used`
Defaulting to a 1 year period seems coherent with the extended lifetime of injected service account tokens.
